He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]]. ==High school career== Williams played basketball for [[R. Nelson Snider High School]] in [[Fort Wayne, Indiana]].{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Neddenriep|title=Recruiting: Malik Williams has 2 offers, interest growing|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/recruiting-central/2015/05/02/fort-wayne-sniders-malik-williams-has-two-offers-and-interest-continuing-to-grow/26763065/|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|date=May 2, 2015|access-date=October 21, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 21.5 points, 12.5 rebounds and four blocks per game, leading his team to its first [[Summit Athletic Conference (IHSAA)|Summit Athletic Conference]] title since 2009. Williams was one of four finalists for the [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] award.{{cite web|title=Snider's Williams a finalist for Indiana Mr. Basketball award|url=https://www.news-sentinel.com/sports/top-sports/2017/04/06/sniders-williams-a-finalist-for-indiana-mr-basketball-award/|work=[[The News-Sentinel]]|date=April 6, 2017|access-date=October 21, 2021}} He left as the program's all-time leader in rebounds and blocks.{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Greer|title=Can Louisville's coaches find a niche for Malik Williams?|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/635238/2018/11/06/can-louisvilles-coaches-find-a-niche-for-malik-williams/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=November 6, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Williams was considered a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[ESPN]], and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On August 4, 2016, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] over offers from [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], among others.{{cite web|first=Ricky|last=O'Donnell|title=4-star recruit Malik Williams commits to Louisville amid NCAA scandal|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/8/4/12380118/4-star-recruit-malik-williams-commits-to-louisville-amid-ncaa-scandal|work=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 4, 2016|access-date=October 21, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Greer|title=Recruiting analyst breaks down new U of L pledge|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2016/08/05/recruiting-analyst-jerry-meyer-breaks-down-new-louisville-basketball-commit-malik-williams/88226750/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=August 5, 2016|access-date=October 21, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Rutherford|title=Malik Williams a 5-star prospect in final ESPN class of 2017 rankings|url=https://www.cardchronicle.com/2017/4/18/15341116/malik-williams-a-5-star-prospect-in-final-espn-class-of-2017-rankings|website=CardChronicle.com|date=April 18, 2017|access-date=October 21, 2021}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Malik Williams | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] / [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Fort Wayne, Indiana|Fort Wayne, IN]] | highschool = [[R. Meet Malik Williams.|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/08/22/louisville-basketball-malik-williams-defense-shot-blocking/979178002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=August 22, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2021}} On January 6, 2019, he posted a career-high 19 points and 11 rebounds in a 90–73 win against [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]].{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Sullivan|title=Why Louisville basketball's Malik Williams has earned a longer look|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2019/01/07/louisville-basketball-malik-williams-has-earned-longer-look/2499125002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=January 7, 2019|access-date=October 21, 2021}} Williams averaged 7.7 points and 6.1 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Drautsep|title=Williams out for 6 to 8 weeks|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/williams-out-broken-foot|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=September 23, 2019|access-date=October 21, 2021}} He missed the first four games of his junior season after undergoing surgery for a broken foot.{{cite web|first=Lucas|last=Aulbach|title=Malik Williams is back for Louisville basketball – and that should worry opponents|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2019/11/22/louisville-basketball-malik-williams-will-make-impact-after-broken-foot/4273573002/|work=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=October 21, 2021}} As a junior, Williams averaged 8.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game, and was the runner-up for [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web|title=Louisville's Malik Williams out 12 weeks; needs foot surgery|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/11/07/louisvilles-malik-williams-out-12-weeks-needs-foot-surgery/114726440/|work=[[USA Today]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 7, 2020|access-date=October 21, 2021}} He was limited to three games in his senior season after reinjuring his foot twice. He returned to Louisville for his fifth season of eligibility, granted due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|first=Matthew|last=McGavic|title=Malik Williams to Return for Fifth Year With Louisville|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/malik-williams-returns|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 20, 2021|access-date=October 21, 2021}} On February 1, 2022, Williams was indefinitely suspended due to failing to uphold program standards, but was reinstated on February 7 after missing two games.{{cite news|title=Louisville Cardinals' top scorer Malik Williams reinstated after suspension|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33239035/louisville-cardinals-top-scorer-malik-williams-reinstated-suspension|work=[[ESPN]]|date=February 7, 2022|access-date=February 7, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Anwil Włocławek (2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Williams signed with [[KK Włocławek|Anwil Włocławek]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] on January 1, 2023.{{cite web|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Anwil Włoclawek lands Malik Williams|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/anwil-wloclawek-lands-malik-williams/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=January 1, 2023|access-date=January 1, 2023}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2023–2024)=== On October 30, 2023, Williams joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] as a tryout player,{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2023-24 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}} but was waived on November 8.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Sioux Falls Skyforce Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Sioux-Falls-Skyforce/6/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 28, 2024}} Five days later, he re-joined the Skyforce{{cite web|title=Skyforce Acquires Malik Williams|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-malik-williams|website=NBA.com|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=January 28, 2024}} where he played 33 games and averaged 11.1 points, 9.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists in 23.2 minutes.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN WILLIAMS TO 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-williams-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2024|access-date=April 3, 2024}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024)=== On April 3, 2024, Williams signed a 10-day contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]]. On April 13, he signed with Toronto for the rest of the season.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Raptors Re-Sign Malik Williams For The End Of The Season|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/04/raptors-re-sign-malik-williams-for-the-end-of-the-season.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=April 13, 2024|access-date=April 13, 2024}} ===Return to Sioux Falls (2024–2025)=== On September 11, 2024, Williams signed with the [[Miami Heat]],{{cite tweet|author=Miami HEAT|title=OFFICIAL: The Miami HEAT have signed guard Bryson Warren and center Malik Williams.|number=1833969037287580015|user=MiamiHEAT|date=September 11, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}} but was waived the next day.{{cite tweet|author=Miami HEAT|title=OFFICIAL: The Miami HEAT have waived Bryson Warren and Malik Williams.|number=1834276534120558881|user=MiamiHEAT|date=September 12, 2024|access-date=September 13, 2024}} On October 28, he rejoined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2024-25 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2024-25-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}} ===College Park Skyhawks (2025–2026)=== On September 24, 2025, Williams signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. He was later waived, and joined the Hawks [[NBA G League]] affaliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]]. After an initial [[Exhibit 10]] contract in September, on December 23, 2025, Williams signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on a [[two-way contract]]. During the Tip-Off Tournament with the Hawks' [[NBA G League]] affiliate,{{Cite web |title=Malik Williams Signing |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-malik-williams-to-two-way-contract}} the [[College Park Skyhawks]], Williams averaged 16.2 points and 10.4 rebounds across 14 games.{{Cite web |title=Malik Williams G-League Statistics |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/w/willima05d.html}} He was released from his two-way contract on January 7, 2026.{{Cite web|title=Hawks waiving Malik Williams|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/hawks-waiving-malik-williams-171059086.html|access-date=January 26, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} Williams had not appeared in any games for the Hawks, but was retained by the Skyhawks. ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== Source{{Cite
